item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR), with generous funding from the Government and People of Japan, has officially opened applications for it’s digital Upskilling and Reskilling Programme 2026. This fully funded initiative is designed to empower Ukrainian women refugees living in Poland and internally displaced women in Ukraine by equipping them with practical digital skills that can unlock employment opportunities, remote work, entrepreneurship, and long-term economic resilience.

As technology continues to reshape industries worldwide, digital skills have become essential for accessing quality jobs and creating sustainable livelihoods. Recognizing this growing need, UNITAR has developed a comprehensive programme that combines technical training, mentoring, coaching, networking, and project development to help participants thrive in the rapidly evolving digital economy.

Approximately 500 women will be selected for the first phase of this prestigious programme, with the highest-performing participants advancing to exclusive hackathons and a final conference where they will present innovative projects before employers, investors, donors, and industry experts.

About the UNITAR Digital Upskilling and Reskilling Programme

The programme aims to strengthen the economic security of Ukrainian women who have been displaced due to conflict by providing practical digital education that aligns with today’s labour market.

Rather than focusing solely on theoretical instruction, participants will gain practical experience through project-based learning, expert mentoring, collaborative workshops, and continuous coaching throughout the programme.

Training will be delivered in:

  • Ukrainian
  • Polish
  • English

The programme is implemented in partnership with:

  • Polish-Japanese Academy of Information Technology
  • Ukrainian Catholic University
  • Eukarya
  • Additional partner organizations committed to supporting Ukrainian women

Why You Should Apply

Successful applicants will have the opportunity to:

  • Learn practical Artificial Intelligence (AI) skills.
  • Build expertise in Geographic Information Systems (GIS).
  • Study AI programming using Python.
  • Develop skills for remote employment opportunities.
  • Improve employability in the technology sector.
  • Create innovative digital solutions.
  • Develop entrepreneurial ideas and socially responsible business concepts.
  • Build a professional portfolio.
  • Learn from experienced instructors and mentors.
  • Join an international professional network.
  • Receive continuous coaching throughout the programme.
  • Compete for selection into the virtual hackathon.
  • Earn the opportunity to present projects before employers and investors.
  • Receive an official UNITAR Certificate upon successful completion.

Programme Structure

The programme consists of three progressive phases that allow participants to continuously develop their technical, entrepreneurial, and leadership skills.

Phase I: Online Digital Training

Approximately 500 participants will begin with an intensive online learning programme.

Every participant will first complete mandatory training in AI Fundamentals before choosing one specialization track.

Participants may choose one of the following tracks:

  • Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
  • AI Programming using Python

Throughout the online training, participants will:

  • Complete online learning modules.
  • Attend weekly webinars.
  • Participate in consultation sessions.
  • Receive personalized coaching support.
  • Work on practical assignments.
  • Build individual digital projects.
  • Create professional portfolios.
  • Develop self-marketing strategies.
  • Design entrepreneurial or employment-focused project plans.

The goal is to ensure every participant finishes Phase I with a practical digital solution or career-ready project.

Phase II: Virtual Hackathon and Workshop

Up to 75 top-performing participants will advance to the second phase.

Selected participants will:

  • Work collaboratively in virtual teams.
  • Solve real-world challenges.
  • Participate in an intensive virtual hackathon.
  • Receive guidance from mentors and industry professionals.
  • Refine projects developed during Phase I.
  • Improve digital solutions using expert feedback.
  • Strengthen business concepts and entrepreneurial ideas.

This phase emphasizes teamwork, innovation, creativity, and practical problem-solving.

Phase III: Final Conference

Approximately 30 outstanding participants will qualify for the final stage.

During this prestigious conference, participants will:

  • Present polished projects.
  • Pitch business ideas.
  • Showcase digital solutions.
  • Engage with employers.
  • Network with investors.
  • Meet donors.
  • Receive additional mentoring.
  • Build leadership skills.
  • Improve communication and presentation techniques.
  • Learn financial planning.
  • Conduct market research for their projects.

The conference provides an excellent platform for participants to gain visibility and establish valuable professional relationships.

Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of the programme, participants will be able to:

  • Apply Artificial Intelligence tools to practical workplace challenges.
  • Improve employability through digital competencies.
  • Use GIS technology to solve real-world problems.
  • Develop AI applications using Python programming.
  • Create digital solutions that address societal challenges.
  • Build professional portfolios.
  • Design project plans.
  • Develop self-marketing strategies.
  • Create socially responsible business concepts.
  • Assess the feasibility and market potential of digital innovations.
  • Collaborate effectively with mentors and peers.
  • Incorporate professional feedback into project development.
  • Deliver compelling project presentations.
  • Demonstrate improved leadership abilities.
  • Strengthen communication skills.
  • Increase confidence in digital technologies.
  • Prepare for careers in technology and entrepreneurship.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements:

  • Be a Ukrainian woman refugee registered in Poland or an internally displaced woman living in Ukraine.
  • Be at least 18 years old.
  • Have an interest in digital technologies.
  • Be motivated to learn through practical experience.
  • Possess basic computer literacy.
  • Have basic mathematics skills.
  • Have access to a computer.
  • Have reliable internet access.
  • Be able to dedicate sufficient time to complete the intensive online programme.
  • Be interested in entering the technology industry or upgrading existing digital skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Applicants are encouraged—but not required—to have:

  • University education.
  • Beginner-level knowledge in an IT-related field.

Importantly, no previous programming experience is required, making the programme accessible to beginners who are eager to learn.

Certification

Participants who successfully complete the programme and satisfy all performance requirements will receive an official UNITAR Certificate.

Training will be delivered through a dedicated digital learning hub that supports:

  • Online learning.
  • Professional networking.
  • Peer collaboration.
  • Resource sharing.
  • Continued access to digital-sector information after programme completion.

About the UNITAR-Japan Partnership

This initiative is made possible through the long-standing partnership between UNITAR and the Government and People of Japan.

The partnership focuses on strengthening resilience, promoting sustainable development, and supporting vulnerable populations through capacity-building initiatives.

Through this programme, displaced Ukrainian women will receive practical digital education that enhances their economic independence while creating opportunities for sustainable employment and entrepreneurship.

Why This Programme Matters

Digital transformation is creating unprecedented opportunities across industries. However, displaced populations often face significant barriers to accessing quality employment and professional development.

This programme directly addresses these challenges by combining technical education with mentoring, coaching, networking, and project development. Rather than simply teaching digital concepts, UNITAR provides participants with practical experience and professional exposure that can significantly improve their career prospects.

For women seeking to rebuild their lives through technology, this programme offers an excellent opportunity to gain internationally recognized training, expand professional networks, and develop innovative projects with guidance from experts.

Application Deadline

25 August 2026

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline, as late submissions may not be considered.

 APPLY HERE 

For more information about this opportunity visit the UNITAR website HERE

Also visit the OFY Website HERE for more global opportunities

Conclusion

The UNITAR Digital Upskilling and Reskilling Programme 2026 represents a valuable opportunity for Ukrainian women refugees in Poland and internally displaced women in Ukraine to acquire in-demand digital skills without financial barriers. Through comprehensive training in Artificial Intelligence, GIS, and Python programming, participants will strengthen their employability, build entrepreneurial capacity, and gain access to mentoring, networking, and career development opportunities. With its structured learning pathway, practical project work, international partnerships, and official certification, the programme provides participants with the knowledge and confidence needed to pursue meaningful careers in today’s rapidly evolving digital economy. Interested applicants should ensure they submit their applications before 25 August 2026 to be considered for this transformative opportunity.

item.content:encoded:
The 2027 Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships are now accepting Expressions of Interest from exceptional Australian innovators who are developing transformative solutions to some of Australia’s most urgent social and environmental challenges.

Established by the Sidney Myer Fund and The Myer Foundation, the Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships provide outstanding individuals with the time, financial support, expert guidance, mentorship, and professional network needed to significantly expand the impact of their innovative initiatives.

Unlike many funding opportunities that focus on delivering predetermined outputs or strict performance indicators, this Fellowship is designed to give talented innovators the freedom to dedicate twelve months exclusively to advancing existing high-impact projects that demonstrate strong potential for lasting societal and environmental change.

Each selected Fellow receives funding of up to AUD 180,000 over a twelve-month period, allowing them to step away from their regular employment and fully concentrate on developing innovative solutions capable of creating meaningful and scalable impact across Australia.

About the Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships

The Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships were established to encourage bold thinking, innovative leadership, and entrepreneurial approaches to addressing complex societal issues.

The Fellowship recognizes that many groundbreaking ideas require dedicated time, financial security, mentorship, and strategic support before they can reach their full potential.

Rather than funding organizations, the Fellowship invests directly in individuals whose ideas have already demonstrated traction and are ready to move to the next stage of development.

Successful Fellows become part of a growing network of innovators who are committed to creating sustainable, long-term solutions that benefit Australian communities.

Fellowship Themes

Applicants must propose projects aligned with one or more of the following priority themes:

  • Inclusion & Equality
  • Sustainability & Environment, including Climate Change
  • Human, Civil & Legal Rights

Projects should clearly demonstrate how they contribute to solving major challenges within these focus areas.

Fellowship Benefits

Each successful Fellow may receive funding worth up to AUD 180,000, including:

1. Personal Fellowship Stipend

Recipients receive:

  • AUD 140,000 stipend
  • Financial support throughout the twelve-month Fellowship
  • Opportunity to dedicate full-time attention to their project

2. Project Funding

An additional up to AUD 40,000 is available for approved project-related expenses, including:

  • Renting dedicated workspace
  • Professional travel
  • Hiring external consultants or specialists
  • Other approved Fellowship-related costs

Project expenses are reimbursed based on approved expenditure.

3. Professional Development Support

Beyond funding, Fellows gain access to:

  • Quarterly meetings with a panel of experienced experts
  • One-on-one mentorship
  • Networking opportunities with previous Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellows
  • Guidance from Fellowship staff and advisors
  • Access to an influential innovation community

Who Should Apply?

The Fellowship welcomes individuals from diverse professional backgrounds, sectors, and lived experiences.

Applicants are encouraged to submit an Expression of Interest if they are leading innovative projects capable of delivering significant social or environmental impact.

Ideal Projects

Projects should be:

  • High-impact
  • Innovative or uniquely applied
  • Capable of generating measurable outcomes
  • Scalable
  • Sustainable over time
  • Focused on addressing significant Australian challenges

Innovation may involve creating entirely new approaches or adapting proven ideas to new contexts.

Ideal Applicants

Strong applicants typically demonstrate:

  • Significant experience in their field
  • Entrepreneurial thinking
  • A proven record of achievement
  • Passion for their cause
  • Strong professional networks
  • Curiosity and willingness to learn
  • Ability to collaborate effectively
  • Commitment to making the most of the Fellowship experience

Eligibility Requirements

To qualify, applicants must:

  • Be an Australian citizen or permanent resident.
  • Reside in Australia for most of the Fellowship period.
  • Be willing to take a twelve-month sabbatical from their current role.
  • Demonstrate a strong history of achievement.
  • Show entrepreneurial and innovative thinking.
  • Be capable of transforming ideas into practical action.
  • Have established networks related to their project.

Project Eligibility Requirements

Eligible projects must:

  • Be based in Australia.
  • Align with one or more Fellowship themes.
  • Have been in development for no longer than three years.

What Fellows Are Expected to Do

The Fellowship is intentionally flexible.

Rather than requiring recipients to meet rigid performance targets, Fellows are encouraged to use the year to advance their initiatives thoughtfully and strategically.

During the Fellowship, recipients are expected to:

  • Focus full-time on their project.
  • Participate in Fellowship activities.
  • Engage with mentors and advisors.
  • Present a mid-term progress update.
  • Deliver a final presentation at the conclusion of the Fellowship.

Funding Exclusions

The Fellowship does not support:

  • Projects older than three years.
  • Academic research projects.
  • Higher degree coursework or dissertations.
  • Medical research.
  • Disease-specific initiatives.
  • International projects.
  • Scholarships.
  • Sponsorships.
  • Funding hubs or accelerator programs.
  • Creative arts projects.
  • Collaborative applications involving multiple individuals.
  • Organizational applications.
  • Capital campaigns.
  • Endowment campaigns.
  • Fundraising events.
  • Program or service delivery projects without innovation potential.
  • Curriculum or education development projects for schools, universities, or educational institutions.

Application Process

The Fellowship follows a multi-stage selection process designed to identify Australia’s most promising innovators.

Stage 1: Expression of Interest

Applicants submit an online Expression of Interest (EOI) during the application window.

Stage 2: Initial Review

Following the closing date, applications undergo an extensive assessment process.

Stage 3: Shortlisting

Selected applicants are invited to prepare a detailed application.

Stage 4: Interviews

Shortlisted candidates participate in interviews.

Stage 5: Final Selection

Successful Fellows are confirmed following completion of the interview process.

2027 Application Timeline

Applicants should carefully note the official timeline:

  • 13 July 2026 – Expressions of Interest open.
  • 16 August 2026 (11:59 PM AEST) – Expressions of Interest close.
  • Week beginning 19 October 2026 – Shortlisted candidates invited to submit detailed applications.
  • 10 January 2027 (11:59 PM AEDT) – Detailed applications due.
  • February 2027 – Interviews conducted.
  • March 2027 – Successful Fellows announced.

Late submissions will not be accepted under any circumstances, including technical difficulties or personal issues. Applicants are also not permitted to submit additional materials after the application deadline.

 APPLY HERE 

For more information about this opportunity visit the Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships website HERE

You can visit OFY Website HERE for more fellowship programs

Recent Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellows

The Fellowship has supported numerous innovators addressing pressing national issues.

Alicia Kennedy

Founder of Cherished Pets, Alicia Kennedy is developing the Human-Animal Bond ecosystem of care (HABCare), integrating veterinary care with housing, health, and social services to improve wellbeing for vulnerable Australians.

Campbell Costello

Founder of Bush Labs, Campbell Costello is expanding access to portable PCR diagnostic technology for animal diseases in remote and underserved regions, strengthening disease surveillance, food security, and public health.

Zanab Malik

Founder of My Special Needs Dental Home, Zanab Malik is creating a digital platform that equips carers and support workers with specialist oral health guidance for Australians living with profound disabilities.

These examples demonstrate the Fellowship’s commitment to supporting innovative ideas with the potential to create nationwide impact.

Why Apply?

The Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships represent one of Australia’s premier opportunities for innovators seeking the resources and freedom to expand transformative ideas.

Recipients receive generous financial support, mentorship, professional guidance, expert advice, and access to an influential community of previous Fellows, enabling them to focus entirely on scaling initiatives that can improve lives and strengthen Australian society.

If you have an innovative project addressing inclusion, environmental sustainability, climate action, or human rights, this Fellowship provides a unique platform to accelerate your work and maximize long-term impact.

Deadline

Expression of Interest Deadline: 16 August 2026 (11:59 PM AEST)

Late applications will not be accepted.

Conclusion

The 2027 Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships offer a rare opportunity for Australia’s most innovative changemakers to dedicate an entire year to advancing bold ideas capable of solving significant social and environmental challenges. With funding of up to AUD 180,000, extensive mentoring, strategic guidance, and access to a powerful network of innovators, the Fellowship is designed to help individuals transform promising initiatives into sustainable, scalable solutions that deliver lasting benefits across Australia. Eligible innovators are encouraged to carefully review the eligibility criteria and submit their Expression of Interest before the application deadline of 16 August 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Research Participation Program offers current students, recent graduates and eligible university faculty an opportunity to explore research experiences connected to the work of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The programme is administered through the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education, commonly known as ORISE. Available opportunities are published in an online catalogue and managed through Zintellect, ORISE’s application-management platform.

Rather than advertising one single position, the programme provides access to a changing collection of research opportunities. Applicants should visit the official catalogue regularly, use the available filters and review each listing separately to identify projects that match their academic background, research interests and professional goals.

Applications are accepted throughout the year, and additional opportunities are added regularly. However, each individual position may have its own eligibility requirements, application instructions and closing date.

About the CDC Research Participation Program

The CDC Research Participation Program connects eligible applicants with research opportunities associated with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The programme may be relevant to people seeking practical research exposure, experience in a public-health environment or opportunities to apply academic knowledge to real-world scientific and policy questions.

Because the programme contains multiple listings rather than a single recruitment cycle, applicants may find opportunities covering different subjects, locations, educational levels and research areas.

The specific responsibilities, duration and qualifications will depend on the individual opportunity selected from the catalogue.

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that all CDC research opportunities have the same conditions. Every listing should be read carefully before an application is submitted.

Who Should Explore the Current CDC Research Opportunities?

The official programme information states that applications are accepted from:

  • Current students
  • Recent graduates
  • Faculty members at United States colleges and universities

These categories are broad, and the exact academic or professional requirements may differ from one opportunity to another.

For example, one project may be designed for undergraduate students, while another may require a graduate degree, specialised laboratory training or experience in a particular research field.

Some opportunities may be suitable for applicants in areas such as:

  • Public health
  • Epidemiology
  • Biological sciences
  • Laboratory research
  • Environmental health
  • Data science
  • Statistics
  • Behavioural and social sciences
  • Health communication
  • Medicine
  • Health policy
  • Other related disciplines

These subject areas are examples of fields that may be relevant to CDC-related research. Applicants must rely on the official description of each individual opportunity to confirm whether their background is suitable.

How the Opportunities Catalogue Works

The ORISE website provides an online catalogue of current CDC research opportunities.

Applicants can browse the catalogue and use search or filtering functions to identify positions that match their qualifications and interests.

Each listing should normally provide the information needed to decide whether to apply, such as:

  • Project title
  • Research area
  • Host office or programme
  • Required education
  • Applicant eligibility
  • Location or participation format
  • Expected activities
  • Application deadline
  • Required documents
  • Opportunity number
  • Contact details

The exact information available may differ between listings.

Applicants should click the title of an opportunity to open its full description rather than relying only on the summary displayed in the catalogue.

Why Applicants Should Check the Website Regularly

CDC research opportunities are available throughout the year, and new listings may be added at different times.

There is no single annual deadline covering every position.

An applicant who does not find a suitable opportunity during one visit may find a relevant new listing later. For this reason, interested candidates should check the catalogue regularly.

It may be helpful to search using several combinations of keywords, including:

  • Academic discipline
  • Research technique
  • Degree level
  • Public-health topic
  • Geographic location
  • CDC programme area

Applicants should also review opportunities slightly outside their main specialisation. A position may require transferable skills in research, data analysis, writing or project support even when its title does not exactly match the applicant’s degree.

Using Zintellect to Apply

Applications are managed through Zintellect, ORISE’s online application system.

To apply for any listed CDC research opportunity, candidates must first create a Zintellect profile.

To visit the official Zintellect website, CLICK HERE.

Once an account has been created, applicants can use the platform to:

  • Review available opportunities
  • Open full project descriptions
  • Prepare an applicant profile
  • Upload supporting documents
  • Submit applications
  • Monitor the status of submitted applications
  • Apply to additional opportunities when eligible

Applicants should ensure that the information entered into their profile is complete and accurate.

A partially completed profile may delay an application or make it more difficult to demonstrate eligibility.

Step-by-Step Application Process

1. Visit the Official Opportunities Catalogue

Begin by reviewing the current CDC research opportunities on the ORISE website.

Use the catalogue’s search and filter functions to identify relevant listings.

2. Read the Full Opportunity Description

Click the title of the position and examine all sections carefully.

Pay particular attention to:

  • Eligibility
  • Required qualifications
  • Research duties
  • Educational level
  • Location
  • Application deadline
  • Required documents

Do not apply based only on the title.

3. Record the Opportunity Number

Each opportunity may have a reference or opportunity number.

Applicants should save this number because it may be required when contacting ORISE with questions.

4. Create a Zintellect Account

Candidates who do not already have an account must create a profile at Zintellect.

Complete all requested sections before beginning the application.

5. Prepare the Required Documents

The exact requirements will be stated in the selected listing.

Depending on the opportunity, applicants may be asked to submit documents such as:

  • Curriculum vitae or résumé
  • Academic transcripts
  • Personal or research statement
  • Cover letter
  • References
  • Recommendation letters
  • Proof of enrolment
  • Proof of degree completion
  • Writing or research samples

Applicants should not assume that the same documents are required for every position.

6. Submit Before the Individual Deadline

Although programme opportunities are advertised throughout the year, individual listings may close on specific dates.

Applicants should submit early and verify that all uploaded documents are readable and complete.

7. Monitor the Application

After submitting, candidates should continue checking their Zintellect account and email for updates, requests or further instructions.

Important Points to Check Before Applying

Because the catalogue contains multiple research opportunities, conditions may vary significantly.

Applicants should verify the following for every listing:

Eligibility

Confirm whether the opportunity is open to current students, recent graduates, faculty members or another specified group.

Degree Requirements

Check whether the listing requires an undergraduate, master’s, doctoral or professional degree.

Graduation Window

Some opportunities for recent graduates may define how recently the applicant must have completed their degree.

Citizenship or Residency Requirements

The general programme summary provided does not state one universal citizenship rule for every opportunity.

Applicants must check each listing for any citizenship, residency, visa or work-authorisation conditions.

Location and Participation Format

Determine whether the opportunity is:

  • In person
  • Remote
  • Hybrid
  • Based at a particular CDC site
  • Connected to another approved research location

Deadline

There is no single deadline for the whole catalogue.

Each position may have its own closing date.

Financial and Appointment Conditions

The general information provided does not specify a standard stipend, salary, benefits package or appointment duration.

Applicants should review the individual opportunity description for any available information about financial support and programme conditions.

Technical Support

Applicants experiencing technical difficulties with Zintellect may contact:

Zintellect Support: Zintellect@orau.org

When requesting support, applicants should describe the technical issue clearly.

Questions about a particular research opportunity should include the relevant opportunity number so that ORISE staff can identify the correct listing.

Application Deadline

There is no single universal application deadline for all CDC Research Participation Program opportunities.

Applications are accepted throughout the year, and new opportunities are added regularly.

However, individual listings may have specific deadlines. Applicants must follow the date stated in the opportunity they intend to apply for.

Conclusion

The CDC Research Participation Program provides a central route for students, recent graduates and eligible faculty members to explore research opportunities connected to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Because the programme includes a regularly updated catalogue of separate positions, applicants should search the official website frequently and review each opportunity on its own terms.

The most important first step is to create a complete Zintellect profile. Candidates can then explore available projects, compare eligibility requirements and apply directly to opportunities that match their academic and professional background.

The catalogue may change throughout the year, so the absence of a suitable opening today does not mean that another relevant opportunity will not appear tomorrow. Research careers are occasionally built through grand discoveries—but often they begin with the less glamorous art of checking the right webpage at the right time.

For current CDC research opportunities, visit the official ORISE opportunities catalogue and select the title of any listing to view its complete description.

For more information about this opportunity, VISIT HERE.

 

To create an account and submit applications, VISIT HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The German Cancer Research Center is accepting applications for a fully funded PhD position in Translational Cancer Biology at the German Cancer Consortium partner site in Munich, Germany.

The three-year doctoral position will investigate the molecular mechanisms that drive the progression, metastasis and therapy resistance of small cell lung cancer. The successful candidate will combine experimental cancer biology with functional genomics, advanced disease models and computational analysis of large-scale sequencing data.

The position is located in the Department of Translational Oncology at the DKTK partner site Munich, based at the LMU Klinikum Großhadern. The successful applicant is expected to begin in November 2026 and will become part of the DKFZ International PhD Program.

Applicants should hold a master’s degree in molecular medicine, human biology, biochemistry, biology or another closely related life-science discipline. Practical experience in molecular biology and mammalian cell culture is required.

The application deadline is 11 August 2026.

About the German Cancer Research Center

The German Cancer Research Center, commonly known as DKFZ, is one of Europe’s largest cancer research institutions.

Its mission, “Research for a life without cancer,” reflects its commitment to understanding the causes and biological mechanisms of cancer and translating scientific discoveries into improved prevention, diagnosis and treatment.

DKFZ brings together researchers working across multiple scientific disciplines, including:

  • Molecular and cellular biology
  • Cancer genetics and epigenetics
  • Functional genomics
  • Computational biology
  • Immunology
  • Medical imaging
  • Epidemiology
  • Translational oncology
  • Clinical cancer research

Researchers at DKFZ work within an international scientific environment supported by advanced technologies, specialist infrastructure and global research partnerships.

The institution aims to create conditions in which fundamental scientific discoveries can be transformed into practical benefits for patients and public health.

About the German Cancer Consortium

DKFZ works with selected university medical centres through the German Cancer Consortium, known as DKTK.

DKFZ acts as the core centre of the consortium, while partner sites are located in:

  • Berlin
  • Dresden
  • Essen and Düsseldorf
  • Frankfurt and Mainz
  • Freiburg
  • Heidelberg
  • Munich
  • Tübingen

The consortium operates joint translational research centres at university medical institutions across these locations.

Its purpose is to narrow the gap between basic laboratory science and clinical cancer care. DKTK researchers develop and evaluate new approaches to personalised oncology, including strategies related to:

  • Cancer prevention
  • Early diagnosis
  • Molecular classification
  • Targeted treatment
  • Therapy-response prediction
  • Drug resistance
  • Translational research
  • Clinical application

The consortium also supports the education of future medical, clinical and translational scientists and helps establish research pipelines connecting laboratory discoveries with clinical research and wider healthcare innovation.

About the PhD Position in Translational Cancer Biology

The PhD project is based in the Department of Translational Oncology at the DKTK partner site Munich.

The selected doctoral researcher will join a project investigating small cell lung cancer, an aggressive form of lung cancer associated with rapid progression, metastasis and frequent treatment resistance.

The project seeks to understand how molecular and epigenetic regulatory mechanisms influence the behaviour of small cell lung cancer cells.

A particular focus will be placed on MYC-dependent transcriptional and epigenetic regulation of enhancer networks.

Enhancers are regulatory regions of DNA that help control gene expression. Changes in enhancer activity can alter which genes are activated or suppressed in cancer cells. These changes may contribute to tumour development, metastatic behaviour and resistance to treatment.

The project will examine how MYC-dependent enhancer regulation shapes gene-expression programmes associated with:

  • Tumour progression
  • Metastasis
  • Cancer-cell identity
  • Therapy response
  • Treatment resistance
  • Potential therapeutic vulnerabilities

By identifying biological dependencies within these regulatory networks, the research may help reveal new treatment targets for patients with small cell lung cancer.

Translational Focus of the Research

The project is designed to connect mechanistic laboratory research with clinically relevant cancer models.

The doctoral researcher will work with patient-derived systems and preclinical models that more closely reflect the complexity of human disease.

This translational approach is intended to ensure that discoveries made in the laboratory are relevant to future treatment strategies.

The research will combine:

  • Molecular biology
  • Cell biology
  • Biochemistry
  • Functional genomics
  • Genome engineering
  • Three-dimensional cancer models
  • Genetically engineered mouse models
  • Multi-omics analysis
  • Computational interpretation of sequencing data

Although the project includes computational components, its primary focus is experimental laboratory research.

Main Responsibilities

Conduct Molecular and Cellular Experiments

The PhD student will perform molecular biology, cell biology and biochemical experiments using human and murine small cell lung cancer models.

This may involve studying:

  • Gene expression
  • Protein function
  • Cellular signalling
  • Cancer-cell proliferation
  • Tumour-cell survival
  • Metastatic behaviour
  • Therapy response
  • Molecular resistance mechanisms

The researcher will be expected to design experiments carefully, maintain accurate records, interpret results and troubleshoot technical challenges.

Apply CRISPR-Based Genome Engineering

The successful candidate will use CRISPR-based genome-engineering tools to investigate genes and regulatory elements involved in small cell lung cancer.

CRISPR approaches may be used to:

  • Disrupt selected genes
  • Modify regulatory regions
  • Test gene function
  • Identify cancer dependencies
  • Examine enhancer activity
  • Conduct functional genetic screens

Experience with CRISPR is not explicitly listed as mandatory, but applicants should demonstrate a willingness to develop expertise in genome engineering and functional screening.

Develop Advanced Three-Dimensional Cancer Models

The PhD student will help establish and characterise advanced three-dimensional cancer models.

These models may better reproduce tumour structure and cancer-cell interactions than conventional two-dimensional cell culture.

Relevant systems may include:

  • Organoids
  • Spheroids
  • Patient-derived models
  • Other advanced in vitro cancer platforms

The researcher will use these models to investigate tumour biology and treatment response under clinically relevant conditions.

Work With Genetically Engineered Mouse Models

The project includes work with genetically engineered mouse models of small cell lung cancer.

Applicants should therefore be interested in animal-based cancer research and willing to learn the relevant experimental, ethical and regulatory procedures.

Previous experience with mouse models is desirable but is not stated as an absolute requirement.

Analyse Multi-Omics Data

The researcher will help integrate and interpret multiple types of genomic and transcriptomic data.

The datasets may include:

  • Bulk RNA sequencing
  • Single-cell RNA sequencing
  • Spatial transcriptomics
  • ChIP sequencing
  • ATAC sequencing

Bulk RNA sequencing measures gene-expression patterns across a population of cells, while single-cell RNA sequencing provides information at the level of individual cells.

Spatial transcriptomics helps researchers examine where gene-expression patterns occur within tissues. ChIP sequencing and ATAC sequencing can provide information about protein-DNA interactions, chromatin accessibility and regulatory activity.

The PhD student is not necessarily expected to enter the project as an advanced computational scientist. However, interest in learning computational methods is important, and basic experience in genomic-data analysis would strengthen an application.

Present and Publish Research Findings

The doctoral researcher will be expected to communicate findings through:

  • Research-group meetings
  • Departmental seminars
  • National conferences
  • International conferences
  • Scientific manuscripts
  • Collaborative publications

The successful candidate will contribute to high-impact scientific publications and participate in collaborations with leading cancer-research groups.

Required Academic Qualifications

Applicants must hold a master’s degree in a relevant life-science field.

Suitable disciplines include:

  • Molecular medicine
  • Human biology
  • Biochemistry
  • Biology
  • Molecular biology
  • Biomedical sciences
  • Cancer biology
  • Biotechnology
  • A closely related life-science discipline

The master’s qualification should provide sufficient preparation for experimental doctoral research in molecular and translational cancer biology.

Required Research Experience

Applicants should have practical experience in:

  • Molecular biology
  • Mammalian cell culture
  • Laboratory-based experimental research

Candidates should clearly describe the techniques they have used during their degree, thesis, research assistantship or previous employment.

Relevant experience may include:

  • DNA and RNA extraction
  • PCR or quantitative PCR
  • Cloning
  • Western blotting
  • Immunofluorescence
  • Gene-expression analysis
  • Cell viability assays
  • Transfection
  • Microscopy
  • Protein analysis
  • Mammalian cell-line maintenance

The vacancy does not state that applicants must already be experts in every method used by the project.

Desired Skills and Interests

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

  • Strong interest in translational cancer research
  • Interest in molecular mechanisms of gene regulation
  • Curiosity about cancer progression and treatment resistance
  • Willingness to work with mouse models
  • Interest in computational analysis of genomic datasets
  • Ability to work independently
  • Strong motivation
  • Collaborative and team-oriented behaviour
  • Excellent written and spoken English

Basic computational or bioinformatics experience is desirable but not mandatory.

Candidates should be prepared to work in an interdisciplinary environment where experimental and computational researchers collaborate closely.

DKFZ International PhD Program

The successful candidate will join the DKFZ International PhD Program.

The programme provides structured doctoral training alongside the candidate’s research project.

Support may include:

  • Scientific mentoring
  • Professional-development opportunities
  • Transferable-skills training
  • Career guidance
  • Research seminars
  • International networking
  • Access to DKFZ Career Service activities
  • Opportunities to engage with doctoral researchers from different disciplines

The programme is intended to help candidates develop both as independent scientists and as professionals capable of pursuing careers in academia, healthcare, biotechnology or related fields.

Research Environment in Munich

The position is based at the Department of Translational Oncology at LMU Klinikum Großhadern in Munich.

The successful candidate will work in a collaborative environment with access to facilities and expertise at both:

  • The German Cancer Research Center
  • Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität Munich

This arrangement provides access to basic, translational and clinical research communities.

The doctoral researcher will benefit from:

  • Modern laboratory infrastructure
  • Advanced imaging technologies
  • Genome-engineering platforms
  • Next-generation sequencing
  • Organoid and three-dimensional model systems
  • Specialist core facilities
  • Computational expertise
  • Clinical research connections
  • International collaborations

Funding and Employment Conditions

The position is fully funded for an initial period of three years.

The selected candidate will receive a doctoral salary together with the usual applicable social benefits.

The exact salary amount is not specified in the vacancy information provided.

Additional employment conditions include:

  • Thirty days of annual vacation
  • Flexible working hours
  • Possible mobile-working arrangements where compatible with the role
  • Possible part-time arrangements
  • Family-friendly working conditions
  • A subsidised Germany job ticket for public transport
  • Access to international research networks
  • Training and mentoring
  • Career-development support
  • Corporate health-management services

Because the project is primarily laboratory-based, any mobile-working arrangement will necessarily depend on experimental responsibilities.

Expected Start Date and Duration

The position is expected to begin in:

November 2026

The appointment is initially limited to:

Three years

Applicants should be available to relocate to, or work in, Munich for the duration of the doctoral project.

Diversity and Equal Opportunity

DKFZ welcomes applications from talented candidates regardless of:

  • Gender
  • Cultural background
  • Nationality
  • Ethnicity
  • Sexual identity
  • Physical ability
  • Religion
  • Age

Candidates with severe disabilities will receive preference where they have equal suitability for the position.

The vacancy does not state any nationality restriction, meaning international applicants may apply subject to the relevant admission, visa and employment requirements.

Measles-Immunity Requirement

DKFZ is subject to the German Infection Protection Act.

All employees must therefore provide proof of immunity against measles.

Applicants should be prepared to submit the required medical or vaccination documentation if selected.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted through the official DKFZ online recruitment system.

Applications sent by email will not be accepted.

DKFZ also states that application documents submitted by post cannot be returned.

Applicants should prepare materials that clearly demonstrate:

  1. Their relevant master’s degree
  2. Laboratory experience in molecular biology
  3. Mammalian cell-culture experience
  4. Interest in translational cancer research
  5. Motivation to study small cell lung cancer
  6. Ability to work independently and collaboratively
  7. English-language proficiency
  8. Any experience with CRISPR, mouse models or genomic-data analysis

The vacancy information does not list every required application document. Candidates should consult the official online portal for the complete submission requirements.

APPLY HERE

Contact Information

Questions about the scientific project may be directed to:

Dr Lisa Fröhlich
Telephone: (0)89 4400-43962

Applications should not be sent to this contact by email.

Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by:

11 August 2026

Candidates should complete the online application before the final day to avoid technical problems.

Conclusion

The DKFZ PhD position in Translational Cancer Biology offers a fully funded opportunity to investigate the molecular mechanisms driving small cell lung cancer progression, metastasis and therapy resistance.

The project combines experimental molecular biology with CRISPR genome engineering, advanced cancer models, functional genomics and multi-omics analysis. Its translational focus provides the opportunity to connect fundamental discoveries with clinically relevant questions and potential treatment strategies.

The successful candidate will join the DKFZ International PhD Program and work at the DKTK partner site Munich within LMU Klinikum Großhadern. They will receive structured supervision, access to advanced research infrastructure, a doctoral salary, social benefits and opportunities for international scientific collaboration.

Applicants should hold a relevant master’s degree, possess practical molecular-biology and mammalian cell-culture experience, and demonstrate excellent English and a strong commitment to cancer research.

The position is expected to begin in November 2026 and is funded for three years. Applications must be submitted through the online recruitment system by 11 August 2026.

For more information about this opportunity, CLICK HERE.

To discover more opportunities, VISIT HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The global movement to recognize and protect the Rights of Nature continues to gain momentum, and forNature is seeking an experienced professional to play a central role in one of its most ambitious international initiatives. The organization is currently recruiting a full-time Initiative Coordinator based in Panama City, Panama, to support the operational, strategic, institutional, and diplomatic coordination of the initiative advancing the adoption of a United Nations Universal Declaration of the Rights of Nature (UDRoN). This is a unique opportunity for professionals with experience in project coordination, international relations, environmental governance, multilateral diplomacy, and institutional engagement to contribute directly to an initiative with global environmental significance.

The successful candidate will coordinate complex international workstreams involving governments, legal experts, communications professionals, civil society organizations, diplomatic missions, and international institutions while working closely with the Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Panama (MiAmbiente).

About the Initiative

The United Nations Universal Declaration of the Rights of Nature (UDRoN) initiative seeks to advance international recognition of Nature as a subject of rights through the United Nations system.

The Initiative Coordinator will play a critical role in ensuring that all aspects of the initiative progress efficiently by coordinating institutional relationships, facilitating communication among stakeholders, tracking deliverables, and supporting diplomatic and legal processes.

The position sits at the intersection of environmental policy, international diplomacy, legal coordination, strategic communications, and institutional management.

Position Overview

The Initiative Coordinator will serve as the central coordination hub for the initiative.

Working closely with forNature and MiAmbiente, the coordinator will oversee operational implementation while ensuring that all teams remain aligned with project priorities, timelines, and strategic objectives. The role combines project management, stakeholder coordination, diplomatic engagement, documentation, communications management, and international event coordination.Although the position is remote, the successful applicant must be based in Panama City and remain available for meetings with Panamanian institutions, as well as occasional international travel.

Major Responsibilities

The Initiative Coordinator will oversee numerous interconnected workstreams.

1. Coordinate the Entire Initiative Team

The successful candidate will coordinate professionals across multiple disciplines, including:

  • Attorneys
  • Legal advisors
  • Communications specialists
  • Public Relations teams
  • Campaign consultants
  • Digital communications consultants
  • Graphic designers
  • Civil society engagement leads
  • Business engagement leads
  • Institutional advisors

Responsibilities include:

  • Acting as the central coordination point
  • Organizing internal workflows
  • Monitoring deadlines
  • Tracking assignments
  • Coordinating deliverables
  • Ensuring smooth communication across all teams
  • Monitoring approvals
  • Supporting strategic decision-making
  • Facilitating collaboration across departments

2. Lead Cross-Functional Team Coordination

The coordinator will organize and facilitate:

  • Internal meetings
  • Strategic planning sessions
  • Briefings
  • Coordination meetings
  • Follow-up discussions

They will also prepare:

  • Agendas
  • Meeting summaries
  • Action items
  • Briefing notes
  • Follow-up communications

The role requires maintaining alignment across legal, diplomatic, operational, communications, campaign, and institutional workstreams.

3. Serve as the Main Institutional Liaison

One of the most important aspects of this position involves serving as the day-to-day operational liaison between forNature and the Government of Panama.

Responsibilities include:

  • Coordinating with MiAmbiente
  • Working with the Office of International Technical Cooperation
  • Supporting coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
  • Managing institutional documentation
  • Tracking ministerial approvals
  • Following document management procedures
  • Maintaining continuity during government personnel transitions
  • Escalating institutional bottlenecks when necessary

4. Support Multilateral Diplomacy

The Initiative Coordinator will provide operational support for international diplomatic engagement.

Responsibilities include:

  • Preparing briefing materials
  • Developing talking points
  • Coordinating bilateral meetings
  • Supporting Panama’s Permanent Missions
  • Assisting embassies
  • Preparing diplomatic correspondence
  • Monitoring United Nations calendars
  • Tracking General Assembly timelines
  • Monitoring multilateral environmental agreement processes

The coordinator will also maintain records of:

  • Member State engagement
  • Government focal points
  • Expressions of support
  • Pending diplomatic actions

5. Document Production and Knowledge Management

The coordinator will oversee document development and information management across the initiative.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Creating the initiative’s Operations Manual
  • Drafting institutional documents
  • Producing concept notes
  • Preparing FAQs
  • Writing meeting records
  • Maintaining terminology consistency
  • Managing bilingual documentation
  • Tracking document versions
  • Protecting confidential materials
  • Organizing centralized documentation systems

Documentation will be prepared in both English and Spanish.

6. Support the For Nature Coalition of States

The coordinator will help expand and manage the growing Coalition of States supporting the initiative.

Responsibilities include:

  • Maintaining communication with participating countries
  • Tracking engagement records
  • Supporting onboarding processes
  • Preparing participation documents
  • Coordinating announcements
  • Managing membership materials
  • Supporting signing ceremonies during international events

7. Build Relationships with Key Stakeholders

The Initiative Coordinator will engage a broad range of stakeholders including:

  • Government institutions
  • International organizations
  • United Nations agencies
  • Academic institutions
  • Research organizations
  • Development partners
  • Philanthropic organizations
  • Business associations
  • Private sector organizations
  • Professional organizations
  • Legal institutions
  • Cultural institutions
  • Subnational governments

The coordinator will also support engagement with:

  • Civil society organizations
  • Indigenous Peoples
  • Traditional authorities
  • Community leaders
  • Local communities

8. Coordinate International Events

Responsibilities include organizing the initiative’s participation in international meetings and conferences by managing:

  • Side event proposals
  • Concept notes
  • Accreditation
  • Speaker coordination
  • Logistics
  • Official programme registration

9. Promote an Intercultural and Politically Sensitive Approach

The coordinator must ensure that implementation reflects:

  • Respect for Indigenous worldviews
  • Cultural diversity
  • Territorial knowledge systems
  • Diplomatic sensitivities
  • Institutional priorities
  • Political contexts surrounding the Rights of Nature movement

Required Qualifications

Applicants should possess substantial professional experience in areas such as:

  • Project coordination
  • Programme management
  • Institutional coordination
  • Campaign implementation

Candidates should demonstrate the ability to:

  • Coordinate multiple projects simultaneously
  • Manage competing priorities
  • Meet strict deadlines
  • Work independently
  • Communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders
  • Handle confidential information professionally

Essential Skills

Successful applicants should have:

  • Professional fluency in English
  • Professional fluency in Spanish
  • Excellent organizational skills
  • Strong written communication skills
  • Strong verbal communication skills
  • Excellent stakeholder management abilities
  • Experience preparing reports and institutional documents
  • Experience managing calendars and workplans
  • Experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams

Preferred Experience

Additional advantages include experience with:

  • Government institutions
  • International organizations
  • Civil society networks
  • Environmental initiatives
  • Multilateral diplomacy
  • United Nations processes
  • Environmental law
  • Rights of Nature frameworks
  • Diplomatic drafting
  • Institutional relationship management
  • Panamanian public administration

Additional Requirements

Applicants should also possess:

  • A valid passport
  • A valid United States visa
  • Availability for international travel
  • Ability to coordinate across multiple time zones
  • Strong intercultural awareness
  • Respect for Indigenous leadership and governance systems

Work Location

The position is based in:

Panama City, Panama

The work arrangement is:

  • Full-time
  • Remote
  • Attendance at meetings with Panamanian institutions when required
  • Participation in in-person national and international engagements as necessary

The engagement is structured as an independent contractor relationship rather than direct employment.

Compensation

forNature offers:

  • Competitive industry compensation
  • Salary based on qualifications
  • Salary based on years of relevant experience

Application Requirements

Interested applicants should submit:

  • A current CV or résumé
  • A brief cover letter written in either English or Spanish

Applications should be emailed  via (info@fornature.org) with the subject line: Application – Initiative Coordinator

Application Deadline

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

There is no fixed application deadline, and candidates with immediate availability are strongly preferred.

Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since recruitment may conclude once a suitable candidate has been identified.

Equal Opportunity Employer

forNature is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace.

The organization does not discriminate on the basis of:

  • Race
  • Color
  • Religion
  • Sex
  • Gender identity
  • Sexual orientation
  • National origin
  • Age
  • Disability
  • Any other legally protected status

The organization strongly encourages applications from:

  • Women
  • Indigenous professionals
  • Individuals from historically marginalized communities.

learn more about the opportunity HERE

Why You Should Apply

This position offers an exceptional opportunity to contribute to an internationally significant environmental initiative that seeks to shape the future of global environmental governance. Professionals interested in diplomacy, international law, environmental protection, public policy, institutional coordination, and multilateral cooperation will find this role particularly rewarding.

Beyond project coordination, the successful candidate will help facilitate collaboration between governments, international organizations, civil society, and legal experts while supporting one of the most ambitious international efforts to advance the Rights of Nature within the United Nations framework.

The position provides meaningful exposure to global environmental diplomacy, strategic communications, institutional development, and international stakeholder engagement, making it an excellent opportunity for experienced professionals looking to make a lasting impact on international environmental policy.

Conclusion

The Initiative Coordinator position at forNature represents an outstanding opportunity for experienced professionals passionate about environmental governance, international cooperation, and sustainable development. Working closely with Panama’s Ministry of Environment and a broad network of international stakeholders, the successful candidate will coordinate high-level legal, diplomatic, operational, and communications activities supporting the advancement of the United Nations Universal Declaration of the Rights of Nature.With competitive compensation, international exposure, meaningful responsibilities, and the chance to contribute to a transformative global environmental initiative, this role is ideal for professionals who thrive in fast-paced, multicultural environments and are committed to advancing environmental justice and global cooperation.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the National Geographic Society & The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation, Data Visualization, and Mapping Externship 2026, an exciting international opportunity designed for young people who are passionate about environmental conservation, geography, mapping, and data-driven storytelling.

This fully remote, part-time externship provides participants with the opportunity to work alongside experts from two of the world’s leading conservation organizations the National Geographic Society and The Nature Conservancy while developing practical skills in Geographic Information Systems (GIS), community conservation, data visualization, environmental research, and science communication.

Running for eight weeks, the externship offers a flexible schedule requiring approximately 10 hours per week, making it suitable for students and young professionals who want to gain valuable international experience while balancing their studies or other commitments.

Participants who successfully complete the program will also receive a $500 educational stipend to help offset internet and technology costs associated with participation.

About the National Geographic Society & The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation Externship

Environmental challenges such as biodiversity loss, climate change, freshwater scarcity, and marine ecosystem degradation continue to affect communities across the globe. Solving these challenges requires innovative thinkers who can use science, technology, data, and storytelling to create meaningful change.

The National Geographic Society and The Nature Conservancy have partnered to launch this unique externship to equip young people with practical conservation skills while empowering them to address environmental challenges within their own communities.

Participants will learn how geographic information and mapping technologies can be used to understand conservation issues, communicate scientific findings, and influence local action.

Rather than focusing only on theory, the program combines learning with practical application, allowing participants to complete hands-on projects using real-world environmental data.

Externship Overview

The program offers an engaging learning experience with the following features:

  • Duration: 8 weeks
  • Start Date: 14 September 2026
  • Format: Fully remote
  • Commitment: Approximately 10 hours per week
  • Educational Stipend: $500 upon successful completion
  • Meetings: Recorded for flexible participation
  • Eligibility Age: 18–25 years
  • Geographic Eligibility: Open worldwide

Because the externship is conducted entirely online, participants from any country can take part without relocating.

What Participants Will Learn

Throughout the eight-week program, participants will explore major conservation issues while developing technical and professional skills that are highly valued across environmental and sustainability careers.

Major learning areas include:

1. Biodiversity and Community Conservation

Participants will study some of today’s most pressing environmental issues, including:

  • Biodiversity loss
  • Conservation solutions
  • Marine ecosystem protection
  • Freshwater conservation
  • Community-based conservation initiatives

They will also examine the relationship between geography, ecosystems, and local communities.

2. Geographic Information Systems (GIS)

One of the major highlights of the externship is practical training in Geographic Information Systems (GIS).

Participants will gain foundational knowledge of GIS technologies used worldwide to:

  • Collect geographic information
  • Manage environmental datasets
  • Analyze spatial information
  • Create professional maps
  • Support conservation planning
  • Visualize environmental challenges

The program uses Esri GIS mapping tools, one of the world’s leading geographic information platforms.

3. Data Visualization

Participants will learn how to transform complex environmental information into visual stories that communicate conservation challenges effectively.

This includes:

  • Visual mapping
  • Spatial data presentation
  • Interactive storytelling
  • Geographic data interpretation

4. Community Research

Participants will conduct research focused on conservation issues affecting their own local communities.

This includes:

  • Identifying environmental challenges
  • Collecting location-based information
  • Researching local biodiversity concerns
  • Investigating community conservation efforts

5. Public Speaking and Science Communication

Strong communication is essential for conservation leadership.

Participants will build confidence by learning how to:

  • Present research findings
  • Explain complex scientific concepts
  • Deliver engaging presentations
  • Communicate conservation solutions effectively

6. Conservation Storytelling

Using Esri StoryMaps, participants will create engaging digital stories that combine:

  • Maps
  • Images
  • Research
  • Geographic information
  • Environmental narratives

These projects become valuable portfolio pieces for future academic and professional opportunities.

Projects Participants Will Complete

Throughout the externship, participants will work on practical assignments, including:

  • Researching conservation issues in their communities
  • Creating maps using GIS software
  • Visualizing environmental data
  • Developing interactive Esri StoryMaps
  • Presenting conservation solutions
  • Collaborating with conservation experts

Skills Participants Will Gain

By the end of the externship, participants will have developed a broad range of transferable skills, including:

Conservation Literacy

Participants will gain a deeper understanding of:

  • Biodiversity conservation
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Geographic conservation strategies
  • Community resilience

Research Skills

Participants will practice:

  • Primary research
  • Secondary research
  • Data collection
  • Information analysis
  • Insight development

Community-Based Problem Solving

Participants will learn structured approaches for:

  • Identifying conservation gaps
  • Designing realistic environmental solutions
  • Addressing local conservation challenges

Cross-Sector Collaboration

Participants will work with professionals from:

  • National Geographic Society
  • The Nature Conservancy

They will gain valuable exposure to collaborative conservation work involving scientists, communicators, and community organizations.

Portfolio Development

Every participant will produce a professional Esri StoryMap that demonstrates their:

  • Research ability
  • Mapping skills
  • Data visualization expertise
  • Conservation storytelling

This project can strengthen future applications for scholarships, fellowships, internships, employment, and grants.

Systems Thinking

Participants will explore how global environmental challenges affect local ecosystems and communities while developing solutions that connect local action with broader conservation goals.

What Participants Receive

Successful participants will benefit from numerous professional development opportunities, including:

  • Hands-on conservation experience
  • Direct mentorship from National Geographic Society experts
  • Guidance from The Nature Conservancy professionals
  • GIS and mapping training
  • Environmental research experience
  • Science communication skills
  • Public speaking experience
  • Portfolio-ready conservation project
  • International networking opportunities
  • Flexible online participation
  • $500 educational stipend upon successful completion

About the National Geographic Society

Founded in 1888, the National Geographic Society is a global nonprofit organization committed to advancing science, exploration, education, and storytelling.

The organization has:

  • Awarded more than 15,000 grants worldwide
  • Supported research across all seven continents
  • Reached millions of students through educational initiatives
  • Inspired global audiences through science and exploration

About The Nature Conservancy

The Nature Conservancy is one of the world’s leading environmental nonprofit organizations.

Its mission focuses on protecting the lands and waters upon which all life depends while addressing:

  • Climate change
  • Biodiversity conservation
  • Sustainable ecosystems
  • Community resilience

The organization works globally to create a future where both people and nature thrive.

Why You Should Apply

This externship is ideal for young people interested in:

  • Environmental conservation
  • Climate action
  • Geography
  • GIS mapping
  • Sustainability
  • Environmental communication
  • Research
  • Science storytelling
  • Data visualization
  • Community engagement

APPLY HERE

No previous experience in GIS, conservation, or environmental science is required.

Participants only need curiosity, enthusiasm, and a willingness to learn.

Who Should Apply?

The externship is especially suitable for individuals who:

  • Are between 18 and 25 years old
  • Care about environmental issues
  • Want to understand how conservation affects communities
  • Are interested in GIS and mapping technologies
  • Enjoy research and problem-solving
  • Want to build an international professional portfolio
  • Prefer flexible remote learning opportunities
  • Have not previously participated in a National Geographic Society + The Nature Conservancy Externship

Application Process

Interested applicants should submit their applications through the official application platform before the closing date.

Because applications are expected to be highly competitive, prospective participants are encouraged to apply as early as possible.

Important Dates

  • Application Deadline: 30 August 2026
  • Externship Start Date: 14 September 2026
  • Duration: 8 weeks
  • Commitment: Approximately 10 hours per week
  • Mode: Fully remote

Visit HERE to learn more about the National Geographic Society & The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation, Data Visualization, and Mapping Externship 2026

Conclusion

The National Geographic Society & The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation, Data Visualization, and Mapping Externship 2026 offers an outstanding opportunity for young people worldwide to gain practical conservation experience while learning from internationally recognized environmental organizations. Through expert mentorship, GIS training, conservation research, and storytelling, participants will develop skills that are increasingly valuable in careers related to sustainability, environmental policy, conservation science, education, and community development.

Beyond the technical knowledge, participants will build a professional portfolio, expand their global network, and contribute meaningful conservation solutions within their own communities. With a fully remote format, flexible schedule, and a $500 educational stipend, this externship provides an accessible pathway for the next generation of conservation leaders to make a lasting impact.

For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.

The National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) is inviting applications for its Collaborative Research Grants 2026, a prestigious funding opportunity designed to advance knowledge in the humanities through collaborative scholarship. The program supports teams of researchers working together on projects that produce significant interpretive outputs such as books, digital publications, scholarly websites, peer-reviewed journal issues, and other sustainable research resources.

With awards of up to $250,000, this funding opportunity provides scholars and institutions with the resources needed to pursue innovative humanities research that contributes to a deeper understanding of the history and culture of the United States and Western civilization.

About the NEH Collaborative Research Program

The Collaborative Research Program supports teams of scholars engaged in humanities research that addresses important research questions through collaborative approaches. Projects may be based within a single discipline or bring together expertise from multiple fields.

NEH encourages projects that:

* Advance humanities scholarship.
* Incorporate diverse perspectives and approaches.
* Explore new areas of inquiry.
* Foster interdisciplinary collaboration.
* Produce tangible and sustainable scholarly outputs.

Collaborators may come from a single institution or multiple institutions, and international partnerships are welcome provided that scholars at U.S. institutions make substantial contributions to the project.

Funding Categories

The 2026 competition supports three project categories:

1. Planning International Collaboration

Supports the development of international humanities research partnerships and collaborative projects.

Maximum Award:  Up to $50,000

2. Manuscript Preparation

Supports collaborative research leading to scholarly books, edited volumes, and peer-reviewed publications.

3. Scholarly Digital Project

Supports the creation of digital humanities resources, databases, websites, and digital publications that advance humanities scholarship.

Funding Benefits

Successful applicants may receive:

* Funding of up to $250,000 depending on project category.
* Support for collaborative humanities research.
* Resources for manuscript development and publication.
* Funding for digital humanities projects.
* Opportunities to establish international research partnerships.
* Support for interdisciplinary and cross-institutional collaboration.

Expected Project Outputs

Projects must result in a tangible and sustainable product, including:

* Co-authored books
* Edited scholarly volumes
* Themed issues of peer-reviewed journals
* Digital publications
* Scholarly websites
* Digital humanities resources

Outputs should demonstrate meaningful collaboration and contribute to significant humanities research questions.

Eligible Applicants

The program is open to organizations and institutions supporting humanities research teams.

Collaborators may come from:

* Universities and colleges
* Research institutions
* Cultural organizations
* Humanities centers
* Nonprofit organizations

International collaboration is encouraged, but U.S.-based scholars must play a significant role in the project.

2026 Program Priority

For the 2026 funding cycle, proposed projects must focus on:

* The history of the United States
* The culture of the United States
* Western civilization

Applicants should ensure that their projects align clearly with these thematic priorities.

Project Duration

Depending on the funding category, projects may receive support for up to:

Three Years

This allows research teams sufficient time to complete substantial humanities projects and produce high-quality scholarly outputs.

Application Timeline

| Application Opens | July 7, 2026 |
| Application Deadline | September 16, 2026 |

Applicants are encouraged to begin preparations early to allow sufficient time for institutional approvals and registration requirements.

Application Process

 Step 1: Review the Funding Opportunity

Carefully read the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and related application guidance documents.

Step 2: Complete Required Registrations

Applicants must have active registrations with:

* SAM.gov
* Grants.gov

Organizations should verify that their registrations are current before beginning the application process.

Step 3: Prepare the Application

Develop a strong proposal that clearly outlines:

* Research objectives
* Collaborative structure
* Project methodology
* Expected outcomes
* Dissemination plans

Step 4: Submit Through Grants.gov

Applications must be submitted electronically through Grants.gov before the deadline.

Why Apply?

The NEH Collaborative Research Grants represent one of the leading funding opportunities for humanities scholars seeking to undertake ambitious collaborative research projects. Whether developing a major scholarly publication, creating innovative digital resources, or building international partnerships, this program provides the financial support needed to generate lasting contributions to humanities scholarship.

The program also encourages interdisciplinary collaboration and supports projects that bring together diverse expertise to address complex research questions in new and meaningful ways.

Contact Information

Division of Research
National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH)

📧 [collaborative@neh.gov](mailto:collaborative@neh.gov)
📞 202-606-8200

Conclusion

The NEH Collaborative Research Grants 2026 offer a remarkable opportunity for humanities researchers and institutions to collaborate on projects that expand knowledge, generate impactful scholarship, and contribute to a deeper understanding of the United States and Western civilization. With funding of up to $250,000, support for international collaboration, and opportunities to create lasting scholarly resources, this program is ideal for teams seeking to advance innovative humanities research. Interested applicants should begin preparing their proposals now and submit their applications before the September 16, 2026 deadline.
